note.note:
Consult Summary:
- 26-year-old woman presents with a new pruritic, dry, red rash on hands and arms that began a few days ago after swimming; no systemic symptoms; likely dermatitis (irritant contact dermatitis favored), managed with topical steroid, emollients, and OTC antihistamines; follow-up arranged.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Dry, itchy, red skin primarily on arms and hands.
- Onset/duration: Began a few days ago; temporal association with a swimming session.
- Course/progression: Persistent over several days; coconut butter used without relief.
- Triggers/exposures: Recent swimming (has swum previously); increased work stress; possible environmental/weather contribution per patient.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Positive: Pruritus; erythema; fatigue/tiredness.
  - Negative: No fever, no sweating, no vomiting, no diarrhea, appetite normal, hydration adequate, normal bowel and urinary function, no “spots,” no spread to chest/legs/face (per discussion), no bleeding or discharge from skin.
  - Soreness/cracked skin: Not documented.
- Systems review (pertinent negatives as above). No other systemic complaints reported.

Past Medical History:
- No prior history of eczema or dermatitis reported.
- Possible lactose intolerance (self-reported).
- Medications:
  - Microgynon (combined oral contraceptive) — dose/route/frequency not documented. Note: Initial statement “not on any medication” followed by disclosure of Microgynon (conflict noted).
- Allergies:
  - No drug allergies stated.
  - Food intolerance: possible lactose intolerance.
- No other chronic conditions reported.

Social History:
- Occupation: Primary school teacher; reports long working hours and high stress recently.
- Living situation: Lives alone.
- Tobacco: Non-smoker.
- Alcohol: Denies use.
- Recreational drugs: Denies use.

Family History:
- Father: Asthma.
- Mother: Hay fever.
- No known family history of skin disease.

Physical Examination:
- Not performed/documented in transcript.

Investigations:
- None performed/documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Pruritic erythematous dermatitis of hands/forearms, onset after swimming
  - Assessment: Clinical picture consistent with dermatitis. Given timing after pool exposure and distribution, irritant contact dermatitis (e.g., chlorine/pool chemicals) is most likely; allergic contact dermatitis or atopic dermatitis are alternatives. No systemic features.
  - Plan:
    - Start topical steroid cream — specific agent/dose/route/frequency not documented.
    - Regular emollients throughout the day for several days — agent/dose/route/frequency not documented.
    - Consider OTC antihistamines for itch (e.g., Piriton/chlorphenamine or loratadine) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
    - Provide patient information leaflet on dermatitis.
    - Follow up in 1 week if not improving; reassess.
    - Analgesics/painkillers (e.g., acetaminophen) not indicated for this complaint per clinician.
- Issue 2: Work-related stress and fatigue
  - Assessment: Patient reports increased stress and feeling tired; clinician noted stress can contribute to skin symptoms.
  - Plan: Acknowledged during visit; no specific intervention documented today.
- Issue 3: Medication reconciliation
  - Assessment: Discrepancy between initial report of no medications and later confirmation of Microgynon use.
  - Plan: Verify and reconcile medication list at next visit (conflict noted).

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Irritant contact dermatitis (High likelihood): Onset after swimming; hands/arms exposure; pruritic, dry, red skin; absence of systemic symptoms.
- Allergic contact dermatitis (Moderate likelihood): Pruritic erythema limited to exposed areas; potential reaction to pool disinfectants or personal care products, though no new product identified.
- Atopic dermatitis (Moderate likelihood): Pruritus with erythema; family atopy (asthma, hay fever) and recent stress support; less favored due to first episode and specific exposure link.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements:
  - No vital signs.
  - No physical exam description of rash morphology (e.g., scale, vesicles, borders, lichenification).
  - No documentation of drug allergies beyond “none stated.”
  - No detailed medication list beyond Microgynon; doses/routes/frequencies not documented.
  - No pregnancy status or gynecologic history discussed.
- Conflicts:
  - Medication history: Patient initially stated no medications, later confirmed taking Microgynon (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality:
  - Generally clear; minor inaudible/elliptical segments but core clinical details intact.
